shadowing.audio_text: I think the weather in my hometown is one of the things that makes it special. Although summers can be hot, there are usually pleasant evenings when families walk together outside.

part1: Where is your hometown?
What do you like most about the area where you live?
Has your neighbourhood changed in recent years?

part2.cue_card: Describe a place in your hometown that you enjoy visiting.

part3: Why do some people prefer living in cities?
How can public spaces improve a neighbourhood?
Should cities preserve old buildings?
How might towns change in the future?

shadowing.audio_text: Studying is more effective when I set a realistic goal for the day. For example, I might review a short topic, practise speaking for a few minutes, and then write down one thing I want to improve tomorrow.

part1: Do you enjoy studying?
What subject did you like at school?
Do you prefer studying alone or with others?

part2.cue_card: Describe something useful that you learned recently.
bullets: how you felt about learning it

part3: How has technology changed the way people learn?
Should schools teach more practical skills?
Why do some adults stop learning new things?
What makes a good teacher?

shadowing.audio_text: In my free time, I usually choose activities that help me relax after a busy day. Sometimes I meet friends for a walk, but I also enjoy reading because it gives me a chance to slow down and think.

part1: What do you usually do in your free time?
Did you have a hobby when you were younger?
Do you like spending free time indoors or outdoors?

part2.cue_card: Describe a hobby you would like to try.
bullets: what you would need to do it
why you want to try it

part3: Why do people need hobbies?
Are hobbies different for young and older people?
Can a hobby become a job?
How do social media affect hobbies?

shadowing.audio_text: Technology has made communication much faster, especially for people who live far from their families. However, I believe that face-to-face conversations are still important because they allow us to notice feelings more easily.

part1: What technology do you use every day?
Do you often make video calls?
Is there any technology you find difficult to use?

part2.cue_card: Describe a piece of technology that is useful to you.
bullets: why it is important to you

part3: How has technology changed communication?
Do people rely too much on smartphones?
What technology might be common in the future?
Should children have limits on screen time?

shadowing.audio_text: Keeping healthy does not always require a complicated routine. I try to sleep well, drink enough water, and move regularly. These small habits make it easier for me to concentrate when I need to study.

part1: What do you do to stay healthy?
Do you prefer walking or exercising indoors?
Has your daily routine changed recently?

part2.cue_card: Describe a healthy habit that you would like to develop.

part3: Why do some people find healthy habits difficult?
Who should teach children about health?
How can cities encourage people to exercise?
Are people more health-conscious than before?

shadowing.audio_text: Travelling can teach us things that we do not learn in a classroom. When we visit another place, we notice different habits, foods, and ways of life. That experience can make us more open-minded.

part1: Do you enjoy travelling?
How do you usually travel around your city?
Is public transport convenient where you live?

part2.cue_card: Describe a journey that you remember well.

part3: Why do people enjoy travelling?
How can tourism help local communities?
Should governments improve public transport?
Will people travel more in the future?

shadowing.audio_text: This week I focused on speaking more clearly rather than speaking very quickly. I learned that a short pause can help me organise my ideas, and that clear pronunciation makes my message easier to understand.

part1: Do you often set goals for yourself?
What kind of goal is important to you now?
Do you prefer short-term or long-term goals?

part2.cue_card: Describe a goal that you would like to achieve.
bullets: how you will feel if you achieve it

part3: Why do people set goals?
Should schools help students plan for the future?
What can make people give up on goals?
How can people measure progress?
